steps.body: Make ten to add any sum. Remember 8 + 5: fill to ten, add what's left. Now try new numbers.
steps.narration: Make ten to add any sum. Remember eight plus five: fill to ten, then add what's left. Now try new numbers.

widget.prompt: For 7 + 6, fill 7 up to ten. Tap just enough.

commonCounts.feedback: That's only 1 more. 7 needs 3 to make ten.
Almost — one cell still empty. 7 needs 3.

widget.missFeedback: 7 needs 3 more to fill the ten-frame.
widget.successFeedback: 7 and 3 makes ten — now 3 of the 6 are left!

predict.prompt: To add 7 + 6 you'll first fill 7 up to ten. Where do the filling dots come FROM?

options.label: Out of the 6 — it gets split

predict.reveal: Making ten borrows from the OTHER number: the 6 splits into 3-to-fill and 3-left-over. Nothing new appears — the six just changes shape.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents make ten add.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for make ten add must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines make ten add.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 7 needs 3 to make ten; the 6 splits into 3 and 3; 10 + 3 = 13.
Fill 7 to ten with 3, and 3 of the 6 are left: 10 and 3 is 13.

widget.prompt: 7 + 6 = ? (7 needs 3 for ten; then add the 3 left.)

commonErrors.feedback: One short — after the ten, 3 are left: 10 + 3 = 13.
7 needs only 3 for ten, leaving 3 of the 6 — not 4. 10 + 3 = 13.

hints: How much does 7 need for ten?

steps.body: Always fill the **bigger** number to ten. Fewer dots to move, fewer mistakes.
steps.narration: Always fill the bigger number to ten. Fewer dots to move, fewer mistakes.

widget.prompt: For 8 + 6, fill the bigger number 8 up to ten. Tap just enough.

commonCounts.feedback: One cell still empty. 8 needs 2 to make ten.

widget.successFeedback: 8 and 2 makes ten — now 4 of the 6 are left!

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents make ten add.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for make ten add must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines make ten add.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 8 needs 2 to make ten; the 6 splits into 2 and 4; 10 + 4 = 14.
Fill 8 to ten with 2, and 4 of the 6 are left: 10 and 4 is 14.

widget.prompt: 8 + 6 = ? (8 needs 2 for ten; then add the 4 left.)

commonErrors.feedback: 8 needs only 2 for ten, so 4 are left — not 3. 10 + 4 = 14.
One too many — after the ten, 4 are left: 10 + 4 = 14.

hints: How much does 8 need for ten?

explanationVariants: 6 + 7 is the same as 7 + 6. Start with the bigger 7: fill to ten with 3, then 3 left, 10 + 3 = 13.
Flip 6 + 7 to 7 + 6 so you move fewer dots: the answer is 13.

commonErrors.feedback: One short — 7 fills to ten with 3, then 3 left: 10 + 3 = 13.
7 needs only 3 for ten, leaving 3 of the 6: 10 + 3 = 13.

explanationVariants: 9 needs 1 to make ten; the 5 splits into 1 and 4; 10 + 4 = 14.
Fill 9 to ten with 1, and 4 of the 5 are left: 10 and 4 is 14.

commonErrors.feedback: 9 needs only 1 for ten, so 4 are left — not 3. 10 + 4 = 14.
One too many — after the ten, 4 are left: 10 + 4 = 14.

hints: Fill the bigger number, 9, to ten.

takeaways: Fill the bigger number up to ten first.
Split the smaller number to do it.
Add the leftover to ten for the answer.
steps.teaser: next: the make-ten capstone — and why teens are 'ten and some'.

concept.body: Slow it down. 7 + 6: fill 7 to ten with 3. The 6 splits into 3 and 3. Ten and 3 is 13.
concept.narration: Seven plus six: fill seven to ten with three. The six splits into three and three. Ten and three is thirteen.

explanationVariants: 7 fills to ten with 3, and 3 of the 6 are left: 10 + 3 = 13.

widget.prompt: 7 + 6 = ? (7 needs 3 for ten, then add the 3 left.)

commonErrors.feedback: You landed one short. Give 7 three to make ten, then the 3 left over makes 13.
Only 3 are left after making ten: 10 + 3 = 13.
